title: Inside hedge funds' AI agents: Citadel, Bridgewater and Man Group
dek: How three hedge funds use AI for research—and why speed, judgment and trading authority must be measured separately.
evidence: Oct 27 executive interviews plus earlier first-party technical disclosures; no independent comparison of fund alpha or security outcomes
takeaway: Citadel, Bridgewater and Man Group are using agents to extend research capacity, not simply replace analysts. The lasting edge depends on expert knowledge, controlled tools and the ability to challenge AI-generated conclusions.

sections.title: What each firm is doing

bullets.detail: Some teams use agent counterparts to conduct independent research and challenge investment theses. Its disclosed Second Brain prototype updates research notes from filings, earnings calls and meetings; that prototype is not evidence of firm-wide deployment.

Its Pocket Analyst combines investment knowledge, proprietary data, tool use and analyst feedback. AIA Labs is scaling the methods, while leadership remains cautious about unconstrained agent autonomy.

Alpha Assistant can locate internal code, construct signals and run backtests under researcher-approved plans. Leadership warns against “cognitive surrender”: treating a fluent answer as independent research.

Bridgewater: Its Pocket Analyst combines investment knowledge, proprietary data, tool use and analyst feedback. AIA Labs is scaling the methods, while leadership remains cautious about unconstrained agent autonomy.

sections.title: Four takeaways worth remembering

bullets.lead: Expert judgment is a training asset
bullets.detail: On six document-filtering tasks, Bridgewater reports 84.7% accuracy for a specialized Qwen3 derivative versus a 78.2% frontier-model baseline, at 13.8× lower inference cost. Vendor-reported task metrics—not investment returns.

bullets.lead: The capability boundary matters more than the prompt
bullets.detail: Read-only document research and sandboxed backtests are not the same risk as modifying a portfolio or placing an order. Enforce the boundary at tool and identity layers, with approvals for writes.

bullets.lead: Human sign-off can hide AI dependence
bullets.detail: Record an analyst’s initial thesis and assumptions before showing the agent’s recommendation. Compare changes, contrary evidence and alternative methods—not just whether the reviewer clicked approve.

bullets.lead: More backtests do not mean more alpha
bullets.detail: Agentic research increases the number of hypotheses tested, and therefore the risk of false discoveries. Require out-of-sample validation, multiple-testing controls, transaction costs and realistic capacity assumptions.

variants.label: Unbounded

Goal: Find the best trade.

variants.code:
Goal: Challenge an analyst's thesis.
Tools: Read-only sources + sandboxed backtests.
Output: Counterevidence + sensitivities.
Decision: Analyst; no trading permissions.
